root_cause.text: In powerpc hash-MMU SLB preload handling, skipping switch_mmu_context() when prev->mm == next->mm let the per-CPU hardware SLB retain stale entries while the software SLB preload cache had been aged/evicted on another CPU, so later exec-time preload functions reinserted duplicate SLB entries and triggered an SLB multi-hit.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “we don't call switch_mmu_context()” when the mm_structs are the same, which “will cause the HW SLB and SW preload cache to go out of sync,” and the patch removes the redundant exec-time preload paths slb_setup_new_exec() and preload_new_slb_context() that “attempt to load some of the same entries” and led to the multi-hit in preload_new_slb_context -> slb_insert_entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the exported prototype for `preload_new_slb_context()` from the header to narrow or clean up the SLB interface.
intent_record.what: The function declaration `void preload_new_slb_context(unsigned long start, unsigned long sp);` was removed from the header while surrounding SLB-related declarations were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: This stops that function from being declared through this header, preventing other compilation units that include it from using this prototype via the header and indicating the interface is no longer intended to be exposed there.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary local forward declaration of `preload_new_slb_context` to clean up the source without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the standalone function declaration `void preload_new_slb_context(unsigned long start, unsigned long sp);` from the source file, leaving the surrounding code unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not directly alter execution behavior; it eliminates a redundant or unnecessary forward declaration in this compilation unit, assuming the function is declared elsewhere or no longer needed here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the SLB context preload from start_thread() so 64-bit Book3S non-radix threads no longer perform that setup during thread startup.
intent_record.what: The change removes an #ifdef CONFIG_PPC64 block inside start_thread() that conditionally called preload_new_slb_context(start, sp) when CONFIG_PPC_BOOK3S_64 was enabled and radix_enabled() was false, while leaving the load_addr variable declaration intact.
intent_record.how: At runtime, start_thread() no longer preloads a new SLB context for 64-bit Book3S systems using the non-radix MMU path, so thread startup skips that architecture-specific address translation setup step that was previously performed here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the obsolete `slb_setup_new_exec` prototype from the internal header to narrow the exposed interface.
intent_record.what: The function declaration `void slb_setup_new_exec(void);` was removed from the header, while the surrounding declarations remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This stops the header from exposing the `slb_setup_new_exec` prototype to files that include it, reducing the visible interface at compile time; it has no direct runtime effect unless the declaration was obsolete or unused and is being removed from external use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop invoking SLB setup during hash__setup_new_exec() so new exec handling performs only slice setup and avoids incorrect SLB reinitialization.
intent_record.what: The call to slb_setup_new_exec() was removed from hash__setup_new_exec(), leaving only slice_setup_new_exec() in that function.
intent_record.how: At runtime, executing hash__setup_new_exec() will no longer perform SLB setup during a new exec path, so only slice-related setup remains. This prevents the previous exec-time SLB reinitialization behavior from occurring in this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the dedicated new-exec and new-context SLB preloading helpers so those early user-space SLB allocations are no longer performed through these paths.
intent_record.what: The change deletes two functions, slb_setup_new_exec() and preload_new_slb_context(), including their logic for checking SLB preload cache capacity, disabling interrupts, preloading specific user-space addresses into the SLB, issuing an isync barrier, and re-enabling interrupts.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the kernel no longer performs these proactive SLB preloads for new exec or new SLB context setup paths, so executable, mmap, stack, and heap segment entries that were previously inserted early will now not be allocated by these helpers; this removes that preloading behavior entirely rather than adding a replacement in the shown diff.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove redundant declarations of preload_new_slb_context to clean up and narrow its interface without changing behavior.
Remove inappropriate SLB setup calls from execution/thread startup paths so only the necessary slice-related initialization occurs and SLB state is not redundantly reinitialized.

relevance_review.reason: The changes only remove redundant declarations of preload_new_slb_context() to clean up its interface and do not modify SLB preload behavior, MMU context switching, cache aging/eviction, or duplicate SLB entry handling involved in the root cause.

The vulnerability is caused by redundant/incorrect SLB preload handling that can reinsert duplicate stale SLB entries during exec/thread startup. These changes directly remove SLB setup/preload calls from start_thread() and hash__setup_new_exec(), matching the root cause by preventing the problematic reinitialization path that led to SLB multi-hit.

This change only removes an obsolete function prototype from a header to narrow the interface. It does not affect MMU context switching, SLB preload/cache synchronization, or the duplicate SLB entry/multi-hit root cause.

The vulnerability is triggered by exec-time SLB preload paths reinserting duplicate stale SLB entries. Removing the dedicated new-exec/new-context SLB preloading helpers directly eliminates those early preload paths that caused the duplicate insertions, so this change addresses the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This directly triggers SLB setup during exec, reusing the software preload cache even when hardware SLB state may be stale due to skipped switch_mmu_context(), leading to duplicate SLB insertions and multi-hit.

This performs thread-start SLB preloading on exec/startup paths, causing redundant SLB entry insertion based on the software cache despite stale per-CPU hardware SLB contents, matching the root cause.

This is the actual hardware SLB insertion for the exec segment; if preload_add() incorrectly concludes the entry is absent because the software cache was aged/evicted, this line inserts a duplicate stale hardware entry and can trigger SLB multi-hit.
This inserts a userspace SLB entry during exec setup for mmap_base. Under the stale-hardware/desynchronized-software-cache condition, it can create duplicate SLB entries in hardware.

This allocates a user SLB entry during new thread context preload. When switch_mmu_context() was skipped and hardware retained stale entries while the preload cache did not, this line can reinsert an already-present SLB entry.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct hardware SLB insertion on the exec path. When switch_mmu_context() was skipped for same-mm switches, hardware SLB entries could remain stale on a CPU while the software preload cache no longer reflected them, so this allocation could insert a duplicate entry and trigger an SLB multi-hit.

This also performs hardware SLB insertion during exec-related preload handling. Under the desynchronization between retained per-CPU hardware SLB state and the aged/evicted software preload cache, it could recreate an already-present SLB entry.

This preloads a user SLB entry for a new thread context. If hardware retained an old entry because switch_mmu_context() was skipped, while the software cache no longer tracked it, this statement could insert a duplicate hardware SLB entry.

This invokes the exec-time SLB setup path that reuses the software preload state despite possible stale hardware SLB contents on the CPU, enabling the duplicate insertion condition described in the root cause.

This triggers thread-start SLB preload handling on exec/startup paths. That path can allocate SLB entries based on software cache state that no longer matches retained hardware SLB entries, contributing to duplicate insertion and SLB multi-hit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body clearly shows the relevant logic in `start_thread()`: `if (!radix_enabled()) preload_new_slb_context(start, sp);`. This commit only adds a guard to skip SLB preload when the radix MMU is enabled. The root cause provided is different: on hash-MMU, `switch_mmu_context()` could be skipped when `prev->mm == next->mm`, leaving stale per-CPU hardware SLB entries while the software preload cache was aged/evicted on another CPU, so later exec-time preload reinserted duplicate SLB entries and caused an SLB multi-hit. In this snippet, the vulnerable construct would be exec-time SLB preload on hash-MMU, and it is still present because `preload_new_slb_context(start, sp);` still runs whenever `!radix_enabled()` (i.e. hash MMU). Therefore the vulnerable logic is present for hash MMU. However, the specific fix for the stated root cause is not present here; this patch only avoids preload under radix, and does not address the stale/duplicate SLB state problem on hash-MMU described in the root cause.
